exposure: Low-risk vs. not low-risk pregnancies according to national guidelines
cohort: 170 infants born at home as planned and 720,047 infants born at hospital in Finland between 1996 and 2013
finding: Although the rate of planned home deliveries increased in Finland between 1996 and 2013, the majority of these deliveries did not adhere to national low-risk guidelines and were associated with increased neonatal morbidity, including two perinatal deaths.
mod_finding: Infants born at home as planned had an increased rate of hypothermia, asphyxia, and need for invasive ventilation compared to infants born in the hospital.
